n: A message about a severe drought. Under the covenant, drought was one of the warnings that came with disobedience.

f.w: the dearth

n: Judah mourns; her city gates (where people gathered) are lifeless; people sit in black mourning on the ground, and Jerusalem’s cry rises up.

f.w: they are black unto the ground
f.g: Mourning in dark clothes, sitting on the ground.

n: Even nobles send servants for water; they reach the cisterns and find nothing, and come back with empty jars, covering their heads in shame.

f.w: their little ones
covered their heads
f.g: A sign of grief and shame.

n: The ground is cracked because there’s no rain; farmers are dismayed and cover their heads.

f.w: chapt

n: Even a doe gives birth in the field and abandons her newborn because there’s no grass—a heartbreaking image of desperation in nature.

f.w: the hind

n: Wild donkeys stand on bare hills panting for air like jackals; their eyes fail because there’s no vegetation.

f.w: dragons

n: Jeremiah prays for the people: though our sins testify against us, act for the sake of Your name. We have turned away many times; we have sinned against You.

f.w: do thou it for thy name's sake
our iniquities testify against us

n: O Hope of Israel, its Savior in times of trouble, why are You like a stranger in the land, a traveler who stops for just one night?

f.w: O the hope of Israel

n: Why are You like a confused man, a warrior who can’t save? Yet You are among us, Lord, and we bear Your name—don’t abandon us.

f.w: astonied
we are called by thy name

n: God answers: these people love to wander and don’t hold back their feet, so He doesn’t accept them. He will remember their sins and punish them.

f.w: Thus have they loved to wander

n: Again: don’t pray for this people’s welfare.

f.w: Pray not for this people

n: Even when they fast and offer sacrifices, God won’t accept them; instead sword, famine, and plague will come. Ritual without repentance doesn’t move God.

f.w: When they fast, I will not hear their cry
by the sword, and by the famine, and by the pestilence

n: Jeremiah protests: but Lord, the prophets keep telling them, “You won’t see sword or famine; God will give you lasting peace here.” He partly excuses the people as misled.

f.w: I will give you assured peace

n: God replies: those prophets speak lies in My name. I didn’t send them, command them, or speak to them. Their visions are false, their divination worthless—products of their own hearts.

f.w: The prophets prophesy lies in my name
divination

n: Those prophets who promise no sword or famine will themselves die by sword and famine.

f.w: By sword and famine shall those prophets be consumed

n: The people who believed them will lie unburied in Jerusalem’s streets with their families. Following false prophets doesn’t excuse anyone from consequences.

f.w: they shall have none to bury them

n: Jeremiah is told to say: let my eyes overflow with tears night and day, for my people—the virgin daughter—has suffered a terrible wound.

f.w: Let mine eyes run down with tears

n: In the fields lie those killed by the sword; in the city, people dying of hunger. Prophets and priests wander into a land they don’t know—exile.

f.w: go about into a land that they know not
f.g: Or “go about the land without understanding.”

n: The people pray: have You completely rejected Judah? Do You despise Zion? We hoped for peace and healing but found only terror.

f.w: we looked for peace, and there is no good
lothed

n: We admit our wickedness and our ancestors’ sin; we have sinned against You.

f.w: We acknowledge, O LORD, our wickedness

n: For the sake of Your name, don’t reject us or dishonor Your glorious throne (the temple). Remember Your covenant—don’t break it.

f.w: the throne of thy glory
f.g: Jerusalem or the temple, where God’s presence was enthroned.

f.w: break not thy covenant with us

n: Can any of the nations’ idols bring rain? Can the sky give showers on its own? Only You, Lord. So we will hope in You, the Maker of all things. A confession that only God controls life’s blessings.

f.w: Are there any among the vanities of the Gentiles that can cause rain?
we will wait upon thee
